Indicator 3 from the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] measures the proportion of patients who receive a CT scan within two hours of arrival at the hospital, a critical metric for acute surgical care [^src1]. The national average for this indicator across Denmark stands at 30.1% (911 out of 3,027 patients) [^src1]. Because the provided data consists of a single snapshot from 2023, no longitudinal trends can be established; the analysis is strictly limited to cross-sectional comparisons across regions and individual hospitals [^src1].

At the regional level, the Central Denmark Region (Midtjylland) leads with 38.6% of patients scanned within the two-hour window, while the North Denmark Region (Nordjylland) trails at 20.2% [^src1]. The Capital Region (Hovedstaden) and Southern Denmark (Syddanmark) sit near the national average at 30.3% and 28.6%, respectively, whereas Zealand (Sjælland) records 25.1% [^src1]. 

When examining individual hospitals, Bornholms Hospital reports the highest compliance rate at 63.0%, followed by Aarhus Universitetshospital at 45.3% and Herlev og Gentofte Hospital at 42.7% [^src1]. However, Bornholms Hospital's figure is based on a small sample size (17 out of 27 patients), resulting in a wide 95% confidence interval of 42.4% to 80.6% [^src1]. Conversely, Amager og Hvidovre Hospital records the lowest rate among all facilities at just 13.2%, significantly underperforming the national baseline [^src1]. Aalborg Universitetshospital (18.9%) and Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse (20.4%) also fall at the bottom of the rankings [^src1].

A notable outlier in the dataset is Nykøbing F Sygehus, which reports a 50.0% scan rate but with a redacted or unavailable denominator (listed as "#/#") and an exceptionally wide confidence interval of 1.3% to 98.7%, indicating high statistical uncertainty [^src1]. Overall, the data highlights significant disparities in acute CT scan turnaround times, with some major university hospitals like Aarhus performing well above the national average, while others like Amager og Hvidovre and Aalborg lag considerably behind [^src1].
